Nagoji is off-panel. The room matches 17.1: limewashed walls, doorway to the courtyard on the left, low stool, clay cup. There is no text, the hands are sound and the upper-right wall gives plenty of space for both balloons. v01 is rejected: the leaf is a beige mat with a treasure-map dashed line, X marks and islands, which contradicts the green leaf, coast line and shaded square in 17.3 and 17.4.

v02 is acceptable, with one small flaw: the square on the leaf is fully cross-hatched instead of having one corner shaded. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, sharp features, receding curly black hair, plain white cloth, a stylus and a palm-leaf bundle. He sits cross-legged, looking down at the leaf, stylus at his chin. The leaf matches 17.3 and 17.4 v02: the same green leaf with the coast line, the square and the offshore dot. The setting is the same limewashed room seen from the reverse angle: lamp niche on the left, doorway to the courtyard on the right, low stool, clay cup. There is no text, the hands and feet are sound, and the large upper wall gives clear space for both balloons. v01 is rejected: the leaf on the floor is a beige strip with a town plan of buildings and trees, which contradicts Karl's coast sketch in 17.3 and 17.4.

Clean on every hard check. The ear region edit worked: a small flush gold stud on the lobe with nothing hanging. Chin is clean-shaven, the moustache is thick and curled, he wears boots, and his sleeve reaches the wrist. Kayal is bay with black points and no white. Ibrahim shows only his right side and has no scar on it. The ships fly Dutch flags, there is no text or watermark, and the copper sky leaves plenty of room for the caption. Small notes only: the riders are edge-lit rather than true silhouettes, the Indiamen have their sails set, and a tiny white highlight on Nagoji's cheek could read as a sweat glint. v01 and v02 both have a dangling ear drop, so neither works as a backup.

v02 is clean. Circular spyglass vignette on a black surround. The hull's flank shows its yellow painted gunport strake, the ports open (cannon), shut (red lid), open. Tiny sailors in plain off-white and grey shirts and caps haul on ropes, with no blue-coated soldiers. The gilded work on the side strake and stern is abstract scrollwork only, with no letters or monogram. Plain Dutch tricolour, copper sky and sun-glinted sea, matching 18.1. v01 FAILS the no-text check: letter-like gold glyphs ('QUCT') on the strake under the quarter rail. Its blue-coated, tricorned figures on deck also go beyond the script.

Acceptable. De Lannoy is seen from behind on the stern quarterdeck in a Dutch blue coat and black tricorne, with pale hair at the collar, hands clasped behind his back, feet apart and no features. No text, and the sky leaves room for the caption. Minor notes: there is no spyglass vignette, and the low, close camera beside the hull reads less like a view through a glass from the ridge. The upper sky is bluer than the copper sky of 18.1 and 18.2. Neither is a hard-check failure.

Acceptable. The full edit took out the grey jaw stubble that v01 had. Nagoji's chin now reads clean at print size, with only a soft cool shadow along the jaw. The ear is a flush gold stud. Nagoji has the lowered spyglass, sleeves to the wrists, the talwar at his sash, boots, and he rides Kayal (bay, black mane). Ibrahim gestures with sound hands, and his visible right cheek has no scar. The sky gives clear room top-left for Ibrahim's balloon and top-right for Nagoji's. Minor continuity note: Ibrahim's horse is a mid bay here but a dark brown in 18.1. Ibrahim holds the reins more than leaving them loose. Rejected: v01 for jaw stubble, v02 for Ibrahim's scar on his right cheek and for showing the glass raised to the eye rather than lowered.

Clean. Ibrahim matches his sheet: white turban, short grey-flecked beard, LEFT ear-to-jaw scar visible, teal short coat over the pocketed vest, white shoulder cloth and mundu. He looks away to the left, away from Nagoji. Hands are sound. Copper sky and ships match 18.1 and 18.4. No text, and the open sky to the right of his head leaves room for the balloon.

v02 passes all hard checks. The high view looks down from the ridge. Five Maravar riders splash knee-deep through the shallows, and farther inland a slow line of four Kerala bullock carts moves along the track. Each cart is two-wheeled on a single axle, with an arched hood of woven bamboo or palm matting and a pair of humped white zebu under a yoke. The prairie-wagon fault is gone. The Dutch ships fly a plain red-white-blue ensign with no letters, there is no text, and the copper sunset matches page 18. Minor: at this size the riders' heads read as dark round caps or close dark hair rather than turbans, and one rider is on a white horse. This camera puts the sea and sun at frame left, while 19.3 and 19.5 have the sun at right. That is a camera flip, not a contradiction. The panel has no lettering. v01 still fails: four-wheeled canvas covered wagons, an anachronism.

v02 passes. It is a true reverse angle from the water, looking past the largest Dutch ship to the palm-covered Travancore coast and the ridge under a violet-and-rose dusk sky. Along the shoreward rail, a row of small silhouetted figures hold raised spyglasses, and about ten pinpoint lens glints point toward the shore, which is the script beat. The ensign is a plain unlettered tricolour, and the stern carving is a plain shield with no letters or monogram. There is no text and no anachronism. The large open sky at upper left holds both off-panel balloons, with tails toward the left edge where the shore ridge (Ibrahim) lies. Minor: the watchers wear dark navy coats and tricornes. They read as the ship's officers in silhouette, not as envoys, which fits the VOC ship and De Lannoy's blue coat on 18.3. The rendering is slightly more photographic than the inked panels around it. v01 still fails: no spyglass glints and not a reverse angle.

Clean. Ibrahim matches his sheet: white turban, short grey-flecked beard, teal short coat over the pocketed cream vest, striped shoulder cloth. His scar runs from the LEFT ear (frame right) down to the jaw, he glances toward frame right where Nagoji sits, the light is copper and low, and his hands are sound. There is no text, and open sky top-left and top-right holds both balloons. Minor: on close zoom, the tiny out-of-focus hooded bullock cart at the lower right looks four-wheeled, but at reading size it reads as a plain hooded cart.

Minor: Nagoji's gold stud is a tiny round bead set at the very bottom of the lobe (about 4 px wide). At print size it reads as a flush stud, and nothing hangs from it. Ibrahim's hand is spread flat on his own shoulder rather than raised in a wave, which is a literal but valid reading of the script beat.

All hard checks pass. Nagoji wears the commander sheet with sleeves down and a flush gold ear stud with nothing hanging. His chin is clean-shaven and he is barefoot on the mat. Ramayyan matches his sheet, there is no text and there are no chairs. Minor: the script's 'last chiefs drifting out' are not shown, so the hall reads as already empty. Nagoji's talwar shows only as a short brass grip tucked in the sash, more like a dagger hilt. The dusk sky at upper right and the roof and pillar area at upper left give room for both balloons.

The contact sheet /tmp/claude-501/ch11-fix1-sheets/page-20-panel-02.png does not exist, so I read both frames directly. v01 fails: the second seated figure meant to be Nagoji has a full beard (the chin is not clean-shaven), a topknot bun and no rust-red turban, a bare shoulder with a striped shoulder cloth and rudraksha beads instead of the commander sheet's tunic and sash. He also gestures and talks toward Ramayyan, which takes the focus off Ramayyan alone. v02 is clean. Ramayyan matches his sheet (thin sharp features, receding curly hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundle and stylus). He is not looking up from the leaf. Both hands are sound and the leaves carry no text or pseudo-text. Only Nagoji's cream tunic and broad red sash show, cropped at the left edge, which matches 20.1. No face, ear or feet of his are visible, so the ear stud, chin and barefoot checks are not triggered. The dusk hall has lamps, a woven mat, the sea and sunset beyond the open side and the last men walking out, which matches 20.1 and 20.3. No chairs, text, anachronism, blood or noose. Lettering space: the sunset sky upper left (x 0.07-0.45, y 0.02-0.22) and the plain mat lower left (x 0.12-0.40, y 0.55-0.85). Nagoji is off-panel to the left, so his tail goes to the left edge.

Ramayyan matches his sheet and shows the dry, thin smile; his hands, stylus and leaves are sound, and there is no text. The large plain wall at right is ideal for both balloons. Minor: about eight people still sit in the background by the sea-side railing, so the hall is fuller than the empty hall of 20.1, though it still reads as lingering at dusk. A woman with jasmine in a maroon sari is among them; the hall's earlier crowds have similar women, so she does not read as Revathi. The soft, headless foreground shoulder at left (white garment with a red band edged in orange) reads acceptably as the listening Nagoji, though his sash is normally plain red.

Tight shot of Ramayyan's weathered hand closing over a few peppercorns on the woven mat, as scripted. The hand anatomy is sound, and the reaching forearm is long but plausible under foreshortening. There is no text, and the setting matches the same dusk hall. Minor: a brass bowl of peppercorns has been added in the foreground, and the leaf bundle in his other hand is drawn as thin strips. The empty mat at lower right and the dusk sky at upper right can take the single off-panel line. Ramayyan's head is out of frame at top left.

All hard checks pass. Nagoji's stud is a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging, and he has a thick moustache with no beard; his fist rests at the chin. He is barefoot, with sleeves down and the commander sheet. Ramayyan matches his sheet and holds a single leaf whose edges are dark with handling, as scripted. There is no text and the lamplit hall matches 20.1. Minor: Nagoji's talwar is not visible, and a small red cloth corner shows by Ramayyan's far knee. There is room for four balloons in the upper wall and roof band: the plain wall above and left of Nagoji's turban and between the centre pillars, plus the roof and sky at upper right above Ramayyan.

Passes the hard checks: commander sheet, boots, sleeves down, no brand showing, talwar at the hip, thick moustache, shaven chin with only faint shading, four clusters of light with no masts, no text, and sound hands. Minor points: the ear ornament is a small gold ball sitting low on the lobe with a tiny cap. It touches the lobe and does not dangle, so it reads as a stud at print size. The background watchman is not clearly older. His dark vest and hand torch do not match the watchman in 21.4. Open sky at top right takes both captions.

Acceptable. The Goa ghost has the vaulted stone wall, the brazier and the table with iron tools. There are no ropes, no noose and no figures. Ear studs are flush on the lobe. Sleeves are down. Minor points: five clusters of ship lights here against four in 21.1, 21.3, 21.4 and 21.5. He gazes up and to the right, away from the lights, so the lights are not really in his eyes. This close-up shows light stubble on the chin and jaw; it is not a beard, but it goes past the bible's clean-shaven ideal. Open night sky at top left takes both captions.

v03 passes all hard checks. Seen from his left rear: the planted hand is his LEFT hand (palm flat on lichened rock, thumb toward his front, five sound digits). The left sleeve is eased back to the elbow, and a pale, glossy, puckered edge of the brand shows on the inner edge of the left forearm about a hand's width above the wrist, with no letters. The ear has a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging. Thick curled moustache and a clean-shaven chin. Rust-red turban, red sash, cream tunic and trousers, and a brown boot visible, which matches the boots row for 21.3. No text, no sparkle or watermark in any corner, and a large open night sky at upper left for both balloons. Minor faults: a full moon is drawn, but neighbouring 21.1 and 21.4 show only stars and no moon; the nails are not clearly ridged; the brand edge is subtle and reads as pale scar sheen at print size. Rejected: v01's planted hand and brand are on his RIGHT arm (body three-quarter to camera, thumb toward the viewer), so the brand is on the wrong arm. v02 has a four-point generator sparkle in the bottom-right corner, and its palm-down hand has the thumb on the image right with the fingers toward camera, which reads as a right hand.

Acceptable. Faint haze over the second of four clusters of lights. Nagoji's head is turned toward it with brows drawn and eyes narrowed. Boots, sleeves down, no brand, clean chin with faint shading, no text. Minor points: the framing repeats the medium-wide of 21.1 rather than putting his head in the near foreground, and his nostrils are not clearly flared. The ear ornament is a gold ball with a tiny cap at the bottom of the lobe. It touches the lobe and does not dangle, but it is borderline against the flush-stud rule. The watchman's look (white turban, sleeveless cream tunic, fire bowl on a wall) differs from 21.1's watchman. Wide open sky at top centre and right takes all three captions.

v02 is acceptable and fixes v01. It is an extreme wide shot with the tiny seated figure at the bluff edge in the left third. The long dark coast curves away with only one faint lamp. Exactly four clusters of light sit on the sea, with no masts or hulls. A broad band of empty night sky across the top takes the caption. The commander look reads at this scale: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers, brown boots (correct for 21.4 onward). Knees are drawn up with arms on them. There is no text, no watermark, no other figures and no anachronism. No hard check fails. Minor points: at this size the face, ear stud and chin cannot be read, and no talwar is visible. A large bright moon with glitter on the water appears here, while 21.1 and 21.4 show a starry sky with no moon in frame. This is tolerable, since the camera is wider and higher. v01 is not acceptable: the figure is still large, not tiny, and the coast is strung with village lamps.
